This project performs the conversion of the Boone Quartz substation from 34.5kV to 69kV as part of the overall rebuild and conversion of the 34.5kV system. The Boone Quartz substation was constructed with a dual high side transformer and the high side was laid out for 69kV operation in preparation for the conversion. Two 69kV line breakers will be installed at the Boone Quartz substation. Existing 69kV lines and 34.5kV lines already constructed for 69kV operation will be re-configured along with installation of 69kV taps into the Boone Quartz substation to make the change to 69kV. No new load is being added during the conversion to 69kV.
The recommended project is to completely rebuild a 5 mile section of the Bricelyn - Walters 69 kV line with standard T2-477 construction and shield wire.

The new transformer high side voltage is 69/34.5kv; it will need a 0.5 mile tap line built to the substation from the existing 34.5kV system with the future plans of 69kV rebuild. Adding the double-circuit tap to the substation will allow connection to the new transformers. The double circuit tap will provide additional reliability, with switching, to have the ability to separate the parallel transformers in the situation a transformer fails, no load will be lost.

nyiso.Project Name: U-21 and V-22 ACR Line Reconductoring
nyiso.Description: The U-21 and V-22 lines have poletop and cross arm decay as well as woodpecker damage along the entire length of the lines. Lines have experienced tree contacts and lightning strikes requiring addition of shield wire. Solution: Rebuild U21 and V22 lines to 115kV standards. Replace all 594 wood structures with 115 kV standard steel structures, reconductor both U-21 and V-22 lines and install OPGW. Alternative 1: Full re-build of both lines to 69kV standards, all structures would be removed and replaced with steel, OPGW installed. This option is expected to cost 4% less than the proposed solution, it will not be able to address future load growth in the area and increased capacity per the 2050 Load Study. Alternative 2: Only replace the structures that need immediate replacement (Rolling replacement). This option was not selected as this would put significant risk on reliability of the line with an increasing rate of wood structure asset damage year-over-year. The duration and cost would be negatively impacted this approach. Alternative 3: Full re-build of both lines to 115kV standards with advanced conductors. Composite/carbon core conductors did not reduce structure heights/quantities adding to project cost.

pjm.Description: The Crete Energy Venture to St. John 345-kV transmission line project connects the Crete Energy Venture power station in Will County, Illinois, with the St. John area in Indiana. This interregional path has undergone historical re-sagging and multi-driver Regional Transmission Expansion Plan (RTEP) upgrades authorized by PJM Interconnection to optimize grid reliability and market efficiency.

Appalachian Power representatives plan to upgrade the electric transmission grid in Pittsylvania County. The Danville Area Transmission Line Rebuild Project involves upgrading approximately 3 miles of 138-kilovolt (kV) transmission line.

The Conastone to Northwest Reliability Upgrade project involves the reconductoring of two 230kV circuits along an approximately 24-mile stretch through Northern Baltimore County and Harford County, from the Conastone Substation to the Northwest Substation.

This work includes the upgrade of two overhead lines, the replacement of six existing structures, and the addition of two new structures. Additionally, there will be 13 foundation reinforcements, 16 foundation repairs, and numerous steel reinforcements to existing lattice towers. Terminal equipment at the Conastone Substation will also undergo necessary upgrades. BGE has identified a potential need to use helicopter flights to complete a portion or portions of this work in 2026. More information will be provided as it becomes available. Construction for this project began in August 2025.

pjm.Project Name: Chesterfield - Tyler 230 kV transmission rebuild and reconductor project
pjm.Description: Rebuild and reconductor 2.9 miles of overhead transmission line from the Chesterfield Substation to just south of the Tyler Substation in Chesterfield County, Virginia. The operating voltage will remain 230 kV while new structures and higher-capacity conductors replace aging infrastructure, increase ampacity, and support regional data center growth, local generation, and reliability needs through Dominion Energy's supplemental transmission planning process.

The project directly connects PSE&G's Kilmer substation and Lake Nelson substation. Because the lines sit within or interface with PSE&G's territory, PSE&G is responsible for executing the inside-plant modifications, line drops, and terminal equipment upgrades at these stations. The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) is the governing state agency funding and driving this grid expansion. They requested these upgrades under PJM's State Agreement Approach to successfully inject 6,400 MW of offshore wind energy into the regional electric grid

pjm.Project Name: Powell County - Zachariah 69 kV reconductoring-related structural reliability upgrade
pjm.Description: The 16.85-mile Powell County - Zachariah 69 kV line was built in 1954. EKPC identified the line for structural loading concerns associated with single wood-pole structures and 556.5 ACSR wire or larger. The source notes that many lines in the program have previously been reconductored with larger wire without corresponding structural design work; alternatives will be developed to address the remaining structural concerns.

pjm.Project Name: Rob Park - Lincoln 138 kV line rebuild and reconductoring
pjm.Description: The Robison Park - Lincoln 138 kV line is approximately 10.9/7.8 miles long and has 44 structures with open conditions, including rusted legs, damaged insulators, and rusted shield wire. The line does not meet current AEP structural-strength or shield-angle requirements. The upper tower sections were replaced and reconductored in 1968 for 138 kV operation, while the lower sections and foundations date to the original 1928 installation. The remaining 3.1 miles are covered under AEP-2019-IM038 and will be addressed through a future solution.

spp.Project Name: WAPA Shasta-Keswick 230 kV transmission line reconductoring with 795-T16 ACCR
spp.Description: WAPA reconductored the Shasta and Keswick substations and the associated 230 kV transmission facilities with 795-T16 ACCR conductor during 2013-2014. The work addressed N-2 overload risk: loss of both Shasta-Cottonwood 230 kV lines could overload the Shasta-Keswick 230 kV line. The ACCR conductor provides over 2,000 amps, allowing each bay to carry the full 710 MW output of the Shasta power plant. The diameter-equivalent conductor met the existing sag without increasing tension and avoided major structure replacement. ACCR was used for jack-bus and drop-down jumpers; 1590 AAC connected the high-temperature strain bus to terminals not rated for high-temperature operation.
